feature: hexa reports what it actually saw
description: Failed claude-text calls carry the CLI's stated reason, the agentic bench refuses up front when its evidence program is missing, the Hex layers tally honours the grade's exclusions, the session context recognises Python, and subagents whose definitions grant no writing tool run without a worktree.

specs.description: A non-zero exit with a `result` on stdout surfaces that result
specs.given: the claude CLI exits with status 1, writes `{"result":"AWS SSO token expired","terminal_reason":"auth"}` to stdout, and writes nothing to stderr
specs.then: the call fails with an error that contains "exited with 1" and "AWS SSO token expired"

specs.description: With no `result`, the error falls back to `terminal_reason`
specs.given: the claude CLI exits with status 2, writes `{"terminal_reason":"rate_limited"}` to stdout, and writes nothing to stderr
specs.then: the call fails with an error that contains "exited with 2" and "rate_limited"

specs.description: Stderr is still reported alongside the stdout reason
specs.given: the claude CLI exits with status 1, writes `{"result":"model unavailable"}` to stdout, and writes "warning: retry exhausted" to stderr
specs.then: the error contains both "model unavailable" and "warning: retry exhausted"

specs.description: A non-zero exit is never reported with nothing after the colon when the CLI said why
specs.given: the claude CLI exits with status 1, writes `{"result":"AWS SSO token expired"}` to stdout, and leaves stderr empty
specs.then: the error message is not "claude-text exited with 1: " with only whitespace or nothing after the colon

specs.description: `result` takes precedence over `terminal_reason`
specs.given: the claude CLI exits with status 1 and writes `{"result":"token expired","terminal_reason":"error"}` to stdout
specs.then: the error names "token expired" as the reason, and is not built from "error" alone

specs.description: Every non-zero exit carries what the CLI wrote
specs.given: any non-zero exit status, any stderr text, and any stdout JSON whose `result` or `terminal_reason` is a non-empty string
specs.when: hexa makes a `claude-text` call that receives them
specs.then: the error contains the exit status, the stdout `result` if it is present (otherwise the `terminal_reason`), and the stderr text whenever stderr is non-empty

specs.description: A missing evidence program stops the bench before any fixture runs
specs.given: five selected fixtures whose evidence commands all start with `bun`, and no `bun` on PATH
specs.then: the command refuses with an error that names `bun` and all five fixtures, no fixture runs, no model is invoked, and no pass rate is reported

specs.description: When every evidence program is present, the bench runs
specs.given: selected fixtures whose evidence commands start with `cargo` and `bun`, and both programs on PATH
specs.then: the pre-flight check passes and the fixtures run

specs.description: One missing program refuses the whole run and names only the fixtures that need it
specs.given: selected fixtures A and B whose evidence starts with `cargo`, which is on PATH, and fixture C whose evidence starts with `pytest`, which is not on PATH
specs.then: the bench refuses, the refusal names `pytest` and fixture C but not A or B, and none of A, B or C runs

specs.description: A fixture that is not selected does not trigger a refusal
specs.given: selected fixtures whose evidence programs are all on PATH, and an unselected fixture whose evidence starts with `bun`, which is not on PATH
specs.when: the user runs `hexa bench agentic` for the selected fixtures
specs.then: the bench does not refuse because of `bun`, and the selected fixtures run

specs.description: The bench runs nothing unless every evidence program resolves
specs.given: any set of selected fixtures and any PATH
specs.then: if the first program of any selected fixture's evidence command is not found on PATH, no fixture runs and the refusal lists each missing program with the fixtures that need it; otherwise the bench proceeds

specs.description: A file excluded by `analyze.exclude` is left out of the layer tally
specs.given: a project with 70 graded source files, 27 more files under a directory listed in `analyze.exclude`, and all 97 files classifying as Use Cases
specs.then: the Hex layers tally shows Use Cases (70 files)

specs.description: A file excluded by the built-in patterns is left out of the layer tally
specs.given: a project with one adapter file that the grade reads and one adapter-classified file that matches a built-in exclusion pattern
specs.then: the tally counts exactly one file for that layer

specs.description: An excluded file is counted in no layer at all
specs.given: a file that `analyze.exclude` excludes from the grade
specs.then: the file adds to no layer's count, including Unclassified, Domain, Ports, Use Cases and Adapters

specs.description: The tally total equals the number of files graded
specs.given: any project and any `analyze.exclude` configuration
specs.then: the per-layer counts add up to the number of files the grade analysed, and every counted file is one the grade read

specs.description: `pyproject.toml` alone means Python
specs.given: a project root that contains `pyproject.toml` and none of `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod` or `package.json`
specs.then: it shows Language: python

specs.description: `setup.py` or `setup.cfg` alone also means Python
specs.given: one project root that contains only `setup.py` and another that contains only `setup.cfg`, among the manifests named
specs.when: the session context is injected for each
specs.then: both show Language: python

specs.description: A Python manifest does not override a Rust, Go or JS manifest
specs.given: a project root that contains both `pyproject.toml` and `Cargo.toml`
specs.then: it does not show Language: python

specs.description: No manifest is not guessed as Python
specs.given: a project root that contains none of `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod` or `package.json`
specs.then: it does not show Language: python

specs.description: Python is shown exactly when a Python manifest is present and the others are absent
specs.given: any subset of {`pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `package.json`} present at a project root
specs.then: it shows Language: python if and only if the subset contains at least one Python manifest and none of `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod` or `package.json`

specs.description: A project definition with only read tools runs in place
specs.given: `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` in the project, with tools Read, Grep and Glob, on a branch where an editing agent would be blocked
specs.when: a code-reviewer subagent is launched without `isolation: "worktree"`
specs.then: the pre-agent hook allows it, as it does for the fixed read-only types

specs.description: The user's home definition is used when the project has none
specs.given: no `.claude/agents/auditor.md` in the project, and `~/.claude/agents/auditor.md` with tools Read and Grep
specs.when: an auditor subagent is launched without a worktree
specs.then: the pre-agent hook allows it

specs.description: A definition that grants Bash, every tool (`*`), or a tool not known to be read-only is still blocked
specs.given: `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` with tools Read, Grep and Bash (and, separately, one with `tools: "*"` and one with Read and an MCP write tool), on a branch where editing agents are blocked
specs.when: a reviewer subagent is launched without a worktree
specs.then: the pre-agent hook blocks it as before

specs.description: A definition with no tools list, or no definition at all, is treated as before
specs.given: one subagent type whose `.claude/agents/<type>.md` has no `tools` list, and another type that has no definition in the project or in the user's home, neither type in the fixed read-only list
specs.when: each is launched without a worktree on a branch where editing agents are blocked
specs.then: the pre-agent hook blocks both

specs.description: The project definition takes precedence over the home definition
specs.given: a project `.claude/agents/helper.md` with tools Read and Edit, and a home `~/.claude/agents/helper.md` with tools Read only
specs.when: a helper subagent is launched without a worktree on a branch where editing agents are blocked
specs.then: the pre-agent hook blocks it

specs.description: A definition is exempt exactly when it lists tools and every one is a read-only tool
specs.given: any subagent type not in the fixed read-only list, launched without `isolation: "worktree"`, and any definition state: absent, no `tools` list, or any `tools` list
specs.then: it is allowed as read-only if and only if the governing definition (the project's, else the home's) has a `tools` list every entry of which is one of Read, Grep, Glob, LS, NotebookRead, WebFetch or WebSearch; otherwise the hook blocks or warns exactly as it did before this ADR
